  'when','will','with','yet','you','your'
]);

analyze(text):
- Find all matches of the Unicode regex equivalent of Python whoosh's tokenizer pattern `\w+(\.?\w+)*`, where Python's `\w` (Unicode) ≈ letters, numbers, underscore. Use JS: /[\p{L}\p{N}_]+(\.?[\p{L}\p{N}_]+)*/gu

export function or(children)                     // same normalization
export function not(child)

export function phrase(field, words)             // words: array of strings

## Lexer

Scan the query string left to right, producing tokens. Whitespace separates tokens. Special constructs:
- `(` and `)` — paren tokens.
- `"` — starts a PHRASE token: read until the next `"` or end of string (unbalanced quote does NOT error; content runs to end of string).
- `'` — starts a SQUOTE token: read until the next `'` or end of string.
- `[` or `{` — starts a RANGE token: read until the first `]` or `}` (inclusive) or end of string. Remember the opening and closing bracket chars.
- Anything else: a WORD chunk — read until whitespace or one of the special start chars above (so `title:"a b"` lexes as WORD `title:` then PHRASE `a b`; `title:(a b)` as WORD `title:`, `(`, ...).

## WORD chunk processing (in this order)

1. Optional single leading `+` -> strip it (no semantic effect). Optional single leading `-` -> strip; the resulting clause is wrapped in q.not(...).
2. Optional trailing boost: /^\^?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ ... specifically, if the chunk contains a trailing `^N` (N a number), strip `^N` and ignore it. (A standalone chunk consisting only of `^N` attaches to the PREVIOUS clause and is ignored — see parser.)
3. Optional field prefix: if the chunk matches /^([\w.]+):(.*)$/s AND group 1 is in fieldNames, the field for this clause becomes group 1 and the remaining text is group 2; if the remaining text is empty, the field prefix applies to the NEXT clause (e.g. `title:"a b"`, `title:(a b)`). If group 1 is NOT a valid field name, treat the whole chunk (including the colon) as ordinary word text.
4. If the remaining text consists only of `*` characters -> q.every(field).
5. Else if the text contains `*` or `?` -> q.wildcard(field, text.toLowerCase()). (Wildcard text is lowercased; no other analysis. Verified empirically: `HELL*` matches indexed term `hello`.)
6. Else: toks = analyze(text). 0 toks -> q.nullQuery(). 1 -> q.term(field, toks[0]). n -> q.and(toks.map(t => q.term(field, t))). (Multi-token word -> AND. Verified empirically: `foo-bar` matches only docs containing BOTH `foo` and `bar`.)

## PHRASE token

toks = analyze(content). 0 -> nullQuery. 1 -> q.term(field, toks[0]). n -> q.phrase(field, toks). (Strict consecutive positions, slop 0 — handled by the executor.) An immediately following standalone `^N` chunk is consumed and ignored.

## SQUOTE token

Treat content exactly like WORD text (analyze -> null/term/and-of-terms). Verified empirically: `'hello world'` (single quotes) behaves as AND(hello, world), NOT a phrase.

## RANGE token

Inner text between brackets: split on /\s+TO\s+/ (uppercase `TO`). If it splits into two parts: start = part1.trim() lowercased, or null if empty; end = part2.trim() lowercased, or null if empty. startExclusive = opening bracket was `{`; endExclusive = closing bracket was `}`. Result: q.termRange(field, start, end, startExclusive, endExclusive). (Verified: `[AA TO CC]` lowercased bounds; `[aa TO cc]` inclusive both ends; `{aa TO cc}` exclusive both ends.) If no ` TO ` separator is found, treat the inner text as ordinary word text (rule 6 above).

## Parser (precedence climbing)

Grammar with three precedence levels:
- Lowest: OR — explicit operators `OR` and `|` (chunk exactly equal to `OR` or `|`; case-SENSITIVE uppercase only — lowercase `or`/`and` are ordinary words that typically analyze to nothing).
- Middle: AND — explicit `AND`/`&`, the keyword `ANDMAYBE`, AND IMPLICIT ADJACENCY: two consecutive clauses with no operator between them are joined by AND. This is whoosh's actual behavior here (verified: `hello world` with docs `hello` and `world` separately matches neither — only docs containing both).
  - `a ANDMAYBE b` -> q.andMaybe(a, b) (matching-wise it matches only a's docs).
- Highest: NOT — a chunk exactly `NOT` (case-sensitive) preceding a unary clause wraps it in q.not(...). `a NOT b` parses as AND(a, NOT(b)). `NOT a b` = AND(NOT(a), b). Leading `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` with no left operand: just parse what follows (e.g. `AND hello` behaves as `hello`).
- `(` expr `)` groups; inside, the same rules apply (adjacency = AND). Empty group -> nullQuery. A field prefix WORD chunk (like `title:`) immediately before `(` applies that field to all clauses produced inside the group... simpler: apply the field to the group's resulting query is NOT possible since fields are baked in — instead, when a pending field prefix is set, parse the following primary (word/phrase/squote/range/group) with that field as the current default field, then restore. For a group, the field override applies to every leaf parsed inside it.
- A pending field prefix similarly applies to a following PHRASE/SQUOTE/RANGE/WORD.

If the whole query produces no clauses (empty string, all stopwords) -> q.nullQuery().

Operators are only recognized when the chunk is EXACTLY `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `&`, `|`, or `ANDMAYBE`.
